summary: Applies an angle-axis rotation (a2) to an in-place 3x3 matrix (this) using the Rodrigues rotation formula when the axis squared-magnitude is a valid non-zero finite value (FPU flags checked), then extracts Euler angles from the resulting matrix into an output buffer (a3). Always performs the Euler extraction; the rotation step is skipped when the FPU status flags indicate the magnitude is zero or not a number.

local_names.this: 3x3 matrix being rotated and read for Euler extraction

operations.description: Compute the squared magnitude of the rotation vector a2: a2[0]*a2[0] + a2[1]*a2[1] + a2[2]*a2[2].
Test the FPU status word flags (v6 & 0x4100) after the magnitude computation; if flags are set (zero or not-a-number magnitude), skip the whole Rodrigues rotation loop.

Compute sqrt of the squared magnitude, normalize the axis components as -1/sqrt * a2[i], and evaluate sin and cos of the rotation angle sqrt(magnitude); derive the Rodrigues rotation coefficients (1.0 - cos, cross-product and outer-product terms).
Apply the rotation to each of the 3 rows of the in-place matrix (this[0..8], 3 floats per row) using the precomputed Rodrigues terms, reading each row's 3 elements and writing the rotated row back.
Call FloatConvertWrapper after the matrix transform (float/double value conversion used by the Euler extraction path).
Write the negated this[5] value into the first output slot of a3.
If fabs(this[5]) equals 1.0 (gimbal-locked case), compute atan2(-this[6], this[0]) into the second output slot and force the third output slot to 0.
Otherwise extract the remaining Euler angles: atan2(this[2], this[8]) into the second output slot and atan2(this[3], this[4]) into the third output slot.
